recent_posts.title: Worst tech purchases for Linux users including iPhone, DaVinci Resolve and more
recent_posts.summary: A Linux user reflects on their worst tech purchases and software decisions over the years. Key regrets include switching to iPhone (poor Linux interoperability, limited background sync, no real open-source app ecosystem), AirPods (degraded battery and mic quality after 2 years, Bluetooth pairing issues), fitness trackers/smartwatches (notification overload, daily charging burden), DaVinci Resolve (terrible Linux packaging, Nvidia-only GPU support for effects, library version conflicts), a non-standard Bluetooth keyboard with layout issues on Linux, a Nintendo Switch that rarely gets used, and an iPad Mini that failed to justify its use case. The core lesson: Linux users need to carefully vet hardware and software for ecosystem compatibility before purchasing, and buying devices to create a use case rather than filling an existing need leads to regret.

FSF settles the Office Suite debacle, good news on age verification - Linux Weekly News
recent_posts.summary: A Linux and open source news roundup covering several topics: the FSF has sided with Euro Office in the OnlyOffice fork dispute, stating that OnlyOffice's additional restrictions on top of the AGPL are unenforceable; age verification legislation updates show progress with Colorado and California potentially carving out exemptions for open source software and Linux distros, while Proton CEO Andy Yen warns against the broader trend; Ubuntu 26.04 released with Wayland-only Gnome/KDE, Rust core utilities, and various improvements; Mozilla's Firefox AI assistant feature details and their use of Anthropic's model to find 271 security vulnerabilities; and Valve sharing Steam Deck performance data with game developers.

recent_posts.title: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS changes overview including GNOME 50 and Wayland-only support
recent_posts.summary: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS brings a wide range of changes. Visual updates include accent-colored folder icons, a refreshed Yaru theme closer to Adwaita, and a non-translucent dock. Key functional changes include switching to a Rust-based sudo replacement for improved memory safety, password asterisk feedback in the terminal, and a new default terminal (Ptyxis) and system monitor (Resources). Packages are now compiled for AMD64 v3 architecture for potential performance gains on modern CPUs. The software-properties GUI is removed by default, limiting graphical repo management. Telemetry is now opt-in. Ubuntu 26.04 ships GNOME 50, which drops X11 entirely (Wayland-only), brings major Nautilus improvements, headless remote desktop sessions with zero-copy rendering, better NVIDIA support, parental controls, and more. Under the hood, the kernel is Linux 7.0, initramfs switches to dracut, and removable media now mounts under /run/media.

recent_posts.title: Germany's moving to Open Source, Age verification gets worse - Linux weekly News
recent_posts.summary: A weekly Linux news roundup covering: Germany's 'Deutschlandstack' initiative to adopt open standards and open-source software across all federal and local administrations by 2028; a proposed US federal age verification bill that could affect Linux distro developers; the EU's anonymous age verification app; Linux kernel 7.0 release highlights including Rust stabilization, filesystem improvements, and AI-generated code policy; Firefox vs Chrome performance benchmarks on Linux showing Chrome 47% ahead; KDE Plasma sprint outcomes including per-monitor virtual desktops (Wayland only) and gesture customization plans; Linux Mint's next release delayed to end of 2026; Proton 11 beta with updated Wine and game fixes; and Mozilla's open-source AI client Thunderbolt.

recent_posts.title: Open source alternatives to popular productivity apps in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive overview of open-source alternatives to popular proprietary productivity software in 2026. Covers PDF editing (OnlyOffice, PDF Arranger, Papers/Okular), task management (Planify, Super Productivity), note-taking (Joplin, AppFlowy, Anytype, Logseq), team chat (Mattermost, Matrix), email (Thunderbird), and full workspace suites (Nextcloud, Proton Docs, CryptPad, Collabora Online). Also touches on Linux as a Windows replacement and briefly mentions GIMP, Krita, and Inkscape for image editing. All alternatives have Linux clients.

recent_posts.title: Patroncast - S06E15 - The EU's move to Linux isn't for the right reasons, but it will still help
recent_posts.summary: European countries, led by France, are migrating government desktops to Linux and open source software. France has 100,000 machines running Ubuntu and is building a sovereign digital suite (messaging, video conferencing, file storage, document editing) licensed under MIT. The primary drivers are digital sovereignty and cost reduction, not ideological commitment to open source. The author argues this is the 'wrong reason' — fear of US and Russian dependency rather than genuine belief in open source — meaning the move could reverse if geopolitical relations improve. However, the net effect is positive: more investment in Linux, open source software, and EU-hosted infrastructure. Even partial EU adoption could push Linux to meaningful market share, forcing proprietary vendors like Microsoft to become more interoperable. The same sovereignty argument extends to AI: the EU will eventually need sovereign AI solutions built on open source foundations.

recent_posts.title: France is moving to Linux and FOSS ! Linux Weekly News
recent_posts.summary: France's national digital directorate has officially announced a plan to migrate from Windows to Linux and EU-made open-source software, with each ministry required to submit migration plans by autumn 2026. The Gendarmerie already runs ~100,000 Linux machines saving €2M/year. Other news includes Linux distros (Zorin OS, Debian, Solus) taking cautious stances on age verification laws, KDE Plasma 6 reviving the Oxygen and Air themes for 6.7, Mesa adopting an AI disclosure policy requiring humans to be responsible for AI-generated code submissions, a proposed Linux kernel driver to detect malicious USB devices, COSMIC desktop UI toolkit improvements, Anthropic donating $1.5M to the Apache Foundation, Valve improving AMD RADV Vulkan driver VRAM management for systems with 8GB or less, and Wine 10.6 restoring Android driver support and improving DLL loading for game mods.

recent_posts.title: Trouble for OpenSource Office Suites, Wayland fixes 2 major features & other Linux Weekly News
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of Linux and open source news covering several controversies: OnlyOffice vs EuroOffice fork dispute over AGPL licensing and branding terms, Nextcloud partnership suspension, and Collabora staff being removed from the Document Foundation amid governance conflicts over LibreOffice. On the technical side, Wayland gains a merged session management protocol after 6 years and a fractional scaling v2 fix. GitHub Copilot injected ads into pull requests affecting 1.5 million PRs before reversing course. Linux hits 5.33% Steam market share, Ubuntu MATE faces maintainer loss, GNOME drops Google Drive integration, Nvidia adds color management API support using AI-generated code, and Wine may adopt Zink for OpenGL via Vulkan.

recent_posts.title: Linux distribution tier list for 2026
recent_posts.summary: A personal tier list ranking of Linux distributions for 2026, covering Pop OS, Elementary OS, Arch, Fedora, Linux Mint, Manjaro, SteamOS, Bazzite, Nobara, Ubuntu, MX Linux, openSUSE Tumbleweed and Leap, Debian, NixOS, Asahi Linux, KDE Neon, Zorin OS, Gentoo, Tuxedo OS, Solus, Deepin, and EndeavourOS. Rankings are based on the author's desktop use case: stability, up-to-date packages, graphical interfaces, and minimal manual maintenance. Fedora, Linux Mint, and SteamOS land in 'great'; Pop OS, Elementary OS, Arch, Bazzite, Ubuntu, Debian, openSUSE Tumbleweed, Zorin OS, Tuxedo OS, and EndeavourOS in 'good'; Nobara, MX Linux, openSUSE Leap, and NixOS in 'average'; Manjaro, Solus, and Asahi Linux in 'no thanks'; KDE Neon, Gentoo, and Deepin in 'hell no'.
